stem: A living liver donor is being discharged after donation. Which symptom should discharge teaching identify as a reason to call the live donor team?

options.text: Mild postoperative fatigue alone without fever or uncontrolled pain
Routine healing at the incision without redness or drainage
Questions about a previously reviewed pain medication schedule when pain is controlled

explanation.rationale_correct: Living donor discharge instructions require donors to call the live donor team if they develop fever, have uncontrolled pain, experience shortness of breath, or have other urgent concerns.

rationale_incorrect.B: Expected fatigue may occur during healing, but fever is an explicit call-the-team trigger.
rationale_incorrect.C: Uncomplicated wound healing without infection signs does not require urgent team contact.
rationale_incorrect.D: Controlled pain on the prescribed regimen is not the urgent call trigger described in donor discharge teaching.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 7, Living Donation → E. Discharge Teaching → 2.f.i.
primary_anchor.quote_hint: call the live donor team if they Develop a fever

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).

stem: During pretransplant education, a candidate asks whether an active untreated infection would prevent kidney transplantation. What teaching is MOST accurate?

options.text: Untreated current infection is a major contraindication to kidney transplantation
Active infection has no bearing on transplant candidacy if the candidate is on the waitlist
Only pediatric candidates are excluded for untreated infection
Untreated infection is an indication for immediate transplantation without treatment

explanation.rationale_correct: Major contraindications to kidney transplantation include untreated current infection, which must be resolved or appropriately managed before transplantation can proceed safely.

rationale_incorrect.B: Untreated infection is explicitly listed among major contraindications, not an irrelevant factor.
rationale_incorrect.C: The contraindication applies to kidney transplant candidacy generally, not a pediatric-only restriction.
rationale_incorrect.D: Active untreated infection is a barrier to transplant, not an indication to proceed without treatment.

stem: During living donor education and informed consent, which disclosure must clinicians provide about recipient treatment options?

options.text: Alternate procedures or treatments for the recipient, including deceased donor transplantation
A guarantee that living donation is the only legal option for every recipient
The donor's future MELD score after donation
Confidential refusal codes from unrelated deceased-donor offers

explanation.rationale_correct: Living donor education must disclose alternate procedures or treatments for the recipient, including deceased donor transplantation, and that a deceased donor organ may become available before living donor evaluation is complete.

rationale_incorrect.B: Donors must be informed of alternate treatment pathways; living donation is not presented as the sole option.
rationale_incorrect.C: MELD scoring applies to liver allocation candidates, not living donor outcome disclosure.
rationale_incorrect.D: Unrelated deceased-donor refusal codes are not part of living donor informed consent disclosures.

stem: A coordinator is revising liver recipient education on recognizing rejection. Evaluate the following statements:

elements.text: Fever may occur with acute liver rejection.
Jaundice may occur with acute liver rejection.
Recipients should contact the transplant team if they notice signs or symptoms of rejection.
Chronic rejection is generally reversible with a single outpatient steroid dose.

explanation.rationale_correct: Acute liver rejection may present with fever, jaundice, and other symptoms, and patients are taught to contact the transplant team if rejection signs develop. Chronic rejection is generally considered irreversible.

rationale_incorrect.A: Statement III is also correct—patients are instructed to contact the team for rejection symptoms.
rationale_incorrect.C: Statement IV is false; chronic rejection is not described as generally reversible.
rationale_incorrect.D: Statement IV is false; not all four statements are correct.
